subject: physics
title: Uses of electromagnetic waves
key_idea: Each part of the electromagnetic spectrum has practical uses, chosen because of its properties. Radio waves are produced by oscillations in electrical circuits, and when absorbed they induce oscillations of the same frequency in a circuit.

blocks.text: This section covers what each type of electromagnetic wave is used for.
Pick each wave below to see its uses. The second row is Higher tier explanation.

diagram.alt: Pick a type of electromagnetic wave to see its uses and why it suits the job.
diagram.prompt: Pick a type of electromagnetic wave
result_labels: Why it suits the job (Higher tier)

options.label: Radio waves
results: Television and radio broadcasting, communications, satellite transmissions.
They carry information through the air. They are produced by, and absorbed to make, oscillations in electrical circuits.

options.label: Microwaves
results: Cooking food, communications (mobile phones, WiFi), satellite communications.
They carry data (signals) between devices, and their energy is absorbed to cook food.

options.label: Infrared
results: Electric heaters, cooking food, thermal imaging cameras, short-range communication, optical fibres, television remote controls, security systems.
Warm objects emit infrared. Hotter objects emit a greater intensity, so a camera shows different temperatures as different shades or colours.

options.label: Visible light
results: Vision, photography, illumination, fibre optic communications.
Light can carry information along optical fibres, and it is the part of the spectrum our eyes detect.

options.label: Ultraviolet
results: Security marking, fluorescent and energy efficient lamps, detecting forged bank notes, disinfecting water, sun tanning.
Its energy gives useful effects, such as making lamps work and marking or checking security features.

options.label: X-rays
results: Medical imaging of bones, airport security scanners for bags, observing the internal structure of objects.
They pass through soft tissue (and bags) but are absorbed by bone (and by objects of greater density), so an image forms.

options.label: Gamma rays
results: Sterilising food and medical equipment, medical imaging and tracers, detecting and treating cancer (radiotherapy), checking metals.
They are very penetrating and can damage or kill cells and microorganisms.

items: Radio waves and microwaves are used for communications.
Infrared is used for heating, cooking and thermal imaging.
Visible light is used for vision, photography and fibre optic communications.
X-rays and gamma rays are used for medical imaging and treatment.
Each part of the spectrum has its own uses.
Radio, microwaves and visible light carry information.
X-rays and gamma rays are used in medicine.

sections.heading: Why a wave suits its use (Higher tier)

blocks.text: (Higher tier) This section covers giving a brief reason why a type of wave suits its job.

items: X-rays are absorbed by bone but pass through soft tissue (flesh), so bones show on the image.
X-rays pass through the bags at an airport to show the contents, including objects of greater density.
Objects at different temperatures emit different intensities of infrared, so an infrared camera shows temperature differences as different shades or colours.
Gamma rays are used to kill cancer cells, and to sterilise food and instruments by killing microorganisms.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Always link the property of the wave to the job it does.

items: (Higher tier) Explain a use by naming the property that makes the wave suitable.
X-rays are absorbed by bone but pass through soft tissue.
Hotter objects emit more infrared.

blocks.text: This section covers how radio waves are made and detected.

items.meaning: A repeated back and forth movement, such as electrons moving to and fro in a circuit.
A current that continually changes direction.

items: Radio waves are produced by oscillations in electrical circuits.
An alternating current in a transmitter aerial produces radio waves.
The radio waves have the same frequency as the oscillations.
When radio waves are absorbed, they induce oscillations in a circuit, an alternating current with the same frequency as the wave.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of radio transmission and reception in order.
diagram.prompt: Put these steps in order, from the transmitter to the receiver.
steps: An alternating current flows in the transmitter circuit and aerial.
Radio waves of the same frequency are produced.
The receiving aerial absorbs the radio waves.
Electrons in the receiver circuit oscillate, giving an alternating current of the same frequency.

items: Radio waves are produced by oscillations in electrical circuits.
Absorbed radio waves induce an alternating current in a circuit.
The frequency of the waves matches the frequency of the oscillations.

checks.q: Describe how a radio signal in a transmitter produces a signal in a receiver.
checks.a: An alternating current (oscillations) in the transmitter produces radio waves. The waves are absorbed by the receiver and induce an alternating current (oscillations) in the receiver at the same frequency.

checks.q: Explain why X-rays are used to produce images of bones.
checks.a: X-rays are absorbed by bone but pass through soft tissue (flesh).

checks.q: Name one use of infrared waves and one use of ultraviolet waves.
checks.a: Infrared: for example cooking, thermal imaging or a television remote control. Ultraviolet: for example security marking, detecting forged bank notes or disinfecting water.

exam_phrases: the radio waves have the same frequency as the oscillations
X-rays are absorbed by bone but can pass through flesh
different temperatures emit different intensities of infrared

mistakes.wrong: X-rays show bones because they are reflected by bone.
mistakes.right: Reflected is not accepted. X-rays are absorbed by bone and pass through soft tissue.

mistakes.wrong: X-rays pass through tissue, so bones show up.
mistakes.right: 'Pass through tissue' is not enough. Say they pass through soft tissue (skin, muscle, flesh) but are absorbed by bone.

mistakes.wrong: The radio waves make an alternating current in the receiver with a different frequency.
mistakes.right: The induced alternating current has the same frequency as the radio wave.

worked_example.question:
Radio waves form part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Explain how electrical signals in a transmitter produce a signal in a receiver.
answer_points: An electrical current (oscillations) in the transmitter produces radio waves.
The radio waves are absorbed by the receiver, inducing an electrical current (oscillations) in the receiver.
The induced current has the same frequency as the radio waves.
worked_example.tip: If no other mark is earned, one mark is allowed for saying that radio waves transfer information or energy through the air.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Radio waves can be produced by oscillations in electrical circuits and can induce oscillations when absorbed. Brief explanations of why each wave suits its use are also Higher tier.

exam_phrases: to see contents / to show objects of greater density
radio waves are produced by oscillating electrons / alternating current (ac)
current flows up and down in a (transmitting) aerial
the frequency of the radio waves corresponds to the oscillation frequency
gamma rays produced in the nucleus

mistakes.wrong: Radio waves are produced by electrons in circuits.
mistakes.right: This only repeats the question and earns nothing. Say the electrons oscillate: an alternating current flows up and down the aerial.

mistakes.wrong: X-rays and radio waves are both produced by oscillating electrons.
mistakes.right: Radio waves come from oscillating electrons in circuits. X-rays come from electrons changing energy levels in an atom.

mistakes.wrong: X-rays are used on bags because they bounce off the contents.
mistakes.right: X-rays pass through (penetrate) the bags, so the contents can be seen and objects of greater density show up.

worked_example.question:
X-rays and radio waves are part of the electromagnetic spectrum and have different uses.

These radiations are produced in different ways.

X-rays are emitted when electrons within an atom go through energy changes.

Radio waves are produced by electrons in circuits.

Compare X-rays with radio waves.

Your answer should refer to
• the uses of both types of radiation
• the different ways that electrons are involved in producing X-rays and radio waves.
answer_points: X-rays have a high frequency, short wavelength and high energy. Radio waves have a low frequency and long wavelength.
X-rays are used for medical diagnosis (broken bones), radiotherapy and airport security.
Radio waves are used for broadcasting radio and television, communications and satellite transmissions.
X-rays: electrons absorb energy and move to a higher energy level. When they fall back to a lower level they lose a large amount of energy as X-ray radiation.
Radio waves: electrons oscillate in electrical circuits, a current that continually changes direction, up and down in a transmitting aerial.
The frequency of the radio waves matches the frequency of the oscillations.
worked_example.tip: This is a levels question marked on 'Level 1 to Level 3'. Detail on a use of each wave plus one clear production process reaches the top level. No credit is given for repeating the wording in the question.

exam_phrases: alternating currents / oscillations produce (radio) waves / electromagnetic radiation

mistakes.wrong: The transmission line produces radio waves because it carries a high voltage.
mistakes.right: The line carries an alternating current (electrons oscillate). Alternating currents or oscillations produce radio waves.

mistakes.wrong: Two uses of gamma rays are killing cancer cells and treating tumours.
mistakes.right: These are the same use. Give two different ones, such as radiotherapy and sterilising food or instruments.

worked_example.question:
Energy is transferred at high voltages in the national grid.

This house is near to a transmission line.

Explain why radio waves may be produced by the transmission line.
answer_points: The transmission line carries an alternating current, so electrons oscillate.
Alternating currents (oscillations) produce radio waves (electromagnetic radiation).
worked_example.tip: One mark for naming the alternating current or oscillations and one mark for saying that these produce radio waves.
